newsitem.title: USA: Motorola wins right to send NBA scores on pagers.
newsitem.headline: Motorola wins right to send NBA scores on pagers.

text.p: A federal appeals court Thursday threw out an injunction that blocked Motorola Inc. from selling handheld pagers displaying updated scores and statistics of National Basketball Association games as they are played.

The pagers account for only a tiny portion of the technology giant's nearly $28 billion in revenues. But Motorola attorney Herbert Schwartz said the decision, the first of its kind, opened the door to other similar services.

"It certainly would apply to the other sports leagues, and it also has implications for online and Internet services and their ability to transmit facts from sporting events or other activities," Schwartz said in an interview in New York.

The 2nd U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals in New York ruled that Motorola and Sports Team Analysis and Tracking Systems (STATS) have not unlawfully taken NBA's property by transmitting "real-time" NBA scores taken from television and radio broadcasts of games in progress.
The appellate court reversed an injunction issued by a U.S. District Court judge in New York involving a pager sold by Schaumburg, Ill.-based Motorola under the name "SportsTrax."
STATS, based in Skokie, Ill., supplies the game information transmitted to the pagers.

"The NBA claimed one, it was a copyright violation and two, that it was misappropriation of their hot news, or that they had the rights to own the scores and statistics until the game was over," Schwartz said. "This court says 'no.'"
The pager became available in January 1996 for about $200. The initial NBA complaint was filed the following spring, Schwartz said.

The lower court's order had stopped Motorola and STATS from transmitting NBA sports information via the pagers, STATS' site on America Online's computer dial-up service or other means unless they obtained NBA authorisation.
"It's a little thing (for Motorola), but they were very happy with this pager," said Mona Eraiba, an analyst with broker Gruntal & Co. "For (company) sentiment, it's great."
Motorola stock rose 62.5 cents to $66.625 on the New York Stock Exchange.
